target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter third-region drain (sub_0801157E)
target.role: drain the third region and zero its count
target.notes: sub_0801157E, 50 bytes and 23 instructions, one terminator at 0x080115AE. THE THIRD REGION'S SHAPE, PROVEN FROM THIS ROUTINE'S OWN INSTRUCTIONS AND NOT FROM SPACING: count at object + 0x208 as a 32-bit word, elements at object + 0x20C + 4*i so 32 bits wide, and each element is DEREFERENCED and used as a table pointer, so each is a POINTER to a virtual object - the same element type as the other two collections. The offset is built by `movs r0, #0x41` then `lsls r0, r0, #3`, so it is never a literal and never an immediate displacement. THE METHOD CALLED IS AT table + 0x14, a DIFFERENT slot from the first collection's destructor at +0x04, the second's at +0x04, and the reader's search predicate at +0x24, so the slot is part of this region's identity and is not shared blindly. The traversal is BACKWARD, from count-1 down to 0, the same direction as the reader and opposite to the keyed move. THE OPERATION IS A DRAIN, NOT A POPULATION: it calls one virtual method per element and then writes ZERO to the count; it never writes an element and never increments a count. sub_08011732 contains the IDENTICAL drain-and-zero inline at 0x080117CA..0x08011804, so this is a routine concept rather than incidental cleanup. NO POPULATION PATH EXISTS, AND THAT IS THE FINDING: (a) no instruction in the image accesses the region by an immediate displacement, so the address is always computed; (b) EIGHT SITES IN THE IMAGE BUILD THE CONSTANT 0x208, found by scanning every byte for the movs/lsls pair in all its register forms and all its decompositions. Exactly THREE of them are in the collection cluster and use it as object + 0x208 for the object at 0x03001C4C: this routine at 0x0801158A, sub_08011732 at 0x080117CA, and sub_08011B04 at 0x08011B7A. ALL THREE WRITE ZERO TO THE COUNT AND NONE OF THEM WRITES AN ELEMENT. The other five sites - 0x080344CC, 0x08034A6A, 0x0804843E, 0x0804E9AE and 0x08054492 - are in unrelated routines that build the same numeric offset for other structures, and NONE of the eight performs the append shape (read a count at +0, increment, store an element at +4). An earlier revision of this comment claimed only three routines compute 0x208; that was WRONG and is corrected here. (c) a search of the WHOLE IMAGE for a STORED POINTER to the region found ZERO occurrences of object+0x204, object+0x208 and object+0x20C, so no code can reach it through a pointer either and a generic append could not be aimed at it; (d) sub_08011B04 additionally bulk-fills the ARRAY at object + 0x20C with 0x200 bytes through an IWRAM-INSTALLED function pointer - the `bx pc` trampoline at 0x0804912C jumps to whatever is stored at 0x030007A8 - so that call's argument order is NOT statically resolvable and it is the single writer of the array area this work cannot characterise. The count is therefore zero on every readable path, which makes the drain DEFENSIVE and normally a no-op. NO CAPACITY CHECK and NO NULL CHECK. The object's +0x00 is not touched. The first and second collections are not consulted. UNKNOWN: whether the bulk fill writes elements or unrelated data sharing the address range, what table+0x14 means, and what sub_0803DA62 and the global at 0x08072824 do. No semantic name is assigned and nothing is imported from another title.
